newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone-Poulenc shares jump on Rorer unit's profit.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc shares jump on Rorer unit's profit.

text.p: Shares in French chemicals group Rhone-Poulenc jumped by neary eight percent on Monday on the back of a 25 percent profit increase at its 68-percent owned pharmaceuticals unit.
Rhone-Poulenc Rorer earlier said its 1996 earnings rose to $428.7 million from $341.60 million, which dealers said was at the top end of expectations.
At 1250 GMT, Rhone-Poulenc was 12.70 francs higher, or 7.20 percent, at 189 francs after hitting a year high of 191 francs.
Shares in Rhone-Poulenc Rorer were 4.66 percent higher at 442.20 while the blue-chip index showed an advace of 0.28 percent at 2,437.24.
The French chemicals group is due to report its own 1996 results on Thursday.

A poll of 29 financial analysts conducted by Jacques Chahine Finance on January 24 shows an average market expectation of an 1996 earnings per share figure of 8.6 francs, an 28 percent increase from 6.71 francs per share, or 2.134 billion francs in total, in 1995.
A source close to the company told Reuters in early January that the net attributable profit would be some 20 to 25 percent higher, with a 25 to 30 percent increase in operating income.
